news.title: How the US naval blockade, rather than sanctions, is choking Iran
news.summary:
STORY: :: How the U.S. naval blockade is choking Iran more than sanctions

:: Dmitry Zhdannikov, EMEA Energy and Commodities Editor

:: London, England / August 25, 2026

"The markets have been focusing in the past 24 hours on the announcement by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent of new measures, against the Iranian oil industry, against Iran in general, and partners who are helping facilitate purchases of Iranian oil and its financial system. 

The consensus in the market that sanctions, the new announced measures, are pretty weak because we haven't seen any big name or institution placed on the list. China has been the main buyer of Iranian oil for the past decade and has said it would continue cooperation. And essentially, China has ring fenced its institution from any US sanctions. Anyone who is buying Iranian oil, the refineries and institutions which help fund those purchases, they don't have any U.S. exposure. So they are essentially isolated from the, global financial system.

However, there is another very important story happening in parallel here, and it has nothing to do with the sanctions itself.

The since the US military has reestablished a physical blockade of Iranian oil in the Gulf, very little, possibly no tankers at all, with Iranian oil have reached the global markets. And, so it has been going on for six weeks. And as we know, oil is the, lifeline of the Iranian economy.

:: U.S. Central Command

Iran has been under US sanctions and then, lately under European Union sanctions, for over 40 years. And it has survived this pressure for a long, long time. However, we've never faced a moment when all of Iranian oil was as isolated and not flowing.

Yes, there have been sanctions, but oil has always been leaking into the global market one way or another.

:: CENTCOM

So this is what the oil markets are currently talking about: How long Iran can last, with no oil revenues at all, how exactly this military blockade of Iranian exports works? Is it far away from the Iranian shore, or is it quite close to the Iranian shore? And what Iran can do to put an end to this and resume oil exports? These are the key questions that are currently worrying the oil markets."
